title: New amide-functionalised extractants for the separation of Co( ii ) from Ni( ii ) and Mn( ii )
content: This study investigates the use of compounds as solvent extraction agents, with particular emphasis on optimising extraction conditions to enhance both selectivity and efficiency. The separation of Co(ii) from Ni(ii) and Mn(ii)-containing solutions via metalate anion extraction represents a promising strategy for recycling NMC battery cathode materials. This approach exploits the pronounced differences in the tendency of these metals to form chlorido metalate anions in aqueous Cl− media. Under such conditions, Co(ii) exists in equilibrium between its hydrated cationic form and the doubly charged tetrachloridocobaltate anion (CoCl42−), whereas Ni(ii) and Mn(ii) form negligible amounts of anionic Cl− species. Amide-functionalised diamine extractants developed in this work demonstrate high Co(ii) extraction efficiencies, good selectivity over Ni(ii) and Mn(ii), and fast extraction kinetics under highly saline, moderately acidic conditions (10 M Cl−, 0.1 M HCl). Under optimal conditions (10 M Cl−, 0.1 M HCl) using 0.01 M extractant and 0.01 M of each metal ion (0.03 M total divalent metals), extractant L3 extracted 76% of Co(ii) in a single stage, with high selectivity over Ni(ii) (βCo/Ni = 70.2) and moderate separation from Mn(ii) (βCo/Mn = 19.9). Furthermore, Co(ii)/Ni(ii) selectivity can be fine-tuned by adjusting the aqueous phase acidity; above 0.01 M HCl, selectivity remains high for Co(ii), whereas reducing the HCl concentration below this threshold results in a significant increase in Ni(ii) co-extraction. Notably, the structurally inverted isomer L2 successfully lowers the high salinity requirement, achieving 41% Co(ii) extraction at a reduced Cl concentration of 6 M, compared to only 10% for its counterpart L4. Efficient, selective stripping of Co(ii) is achieved using 0.1 M HCl, yielding an average cobalt recovery of 95% over five continuous load–strip cycles while co-extracted Ni(ii) and Mn(ii) are preferentially retained in the organic phase, further enhancing final cobalt purity.
